status: 나그네새 10만 마리 이상 · 겨울철새 수천 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록
habitat: 잡목림, 초원, 고산 풀밭, 논 가까운 풀밭

months.note: 4월과 9~10월 이동기에 논과 둘레 풀밭에서 쉽게 보이고, 남부에서는 겨울에 떠도는 개체도 간혹 보이며, 번식지에서는 5월 중순~8월에 알을 낳는다.

summary: 중부 이남을 봄과 가을에 흔히 지나가는 나그네새로, 잡목림과 초원, 고산 풀밭, 논 가까운 풀밭에 산다. 남부에서는 겨울에 떠도는 개체도 간혹 보인다. 땅 위에서 먹이를 찾는 일이 많고, 번식기 수컷은 일정한 세력권을 갖지만 봄과 가을에는 무리 지어 지내는 때가 많다. 일본, 중국 동북부, 몽골, 시베리아, 캄차카, 티베트 등지에서 번식하며 한배에 알을 3~5개 낳는다.

art.subject: Olive-backed Pipit (Anthus hodgsoni), adult in fresh autumn plumage, as seen at Korean rice-field margins in September–October: crown and upperparts olive-green with only faint dark streaks; bold supercilium, buff to orange-buff in front of the eye and whitish behind it, edged above by a thin blackish line; dark eye-stripe; olive-brown ear-coverts with a small white spot above a black spot at the rear corner; blackish malar stripe; throat buffy-white; breast warm buff with bold black streaks and spots, continuing more thinly along the flanks; belly white. Slender bill, dark brown above with a pale pinkish lower mandible; dark brown eye; pink legs.
art.pose: walking on the ground, foraging in short grass
art.scene: Korean autumn migration: harvested rice paddies and the grassy margins beside them, scrubby woodland beyond; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view walking on the ground: olive-green upperparts with faint streaks, bold two-toned supercilium, warm buff throat and breast with bold black streaks, white belly, pink legs, white outer tail feathers

adult, head detail in side view: olive-green crown, supercilium buff in front of the eye and white behind, dark eye-stripe, buff and olive-brown ear-coverts with a white-and-black rear spot, black malar stripe, slender bill with a pale lower mandible
art.build: Small, slim pipit, 15.5cm, about the length of a sparrow but slimmer, with a horizontal stance; walks on the ground and readily flies up into trees when disturbed. Bill thin, straight and pointed, shorter than the head, the culmen slightly curved. Legs medium length, pink, with a short, curved hind claw. Long tertials almost cover the closed primaries. Tail fairly long and slim, dark with white outer feathers, pumped gently and constantly.
avoid: Do not paint a brown, heavily streaked back like Tree Pipit or Red-throated Pipit; this species is olive-green with faint streaks.
Do not leave out the white-and-black spot at the rear of the ear-coverts.
Do not paint an unstreaked breast; it is boldly streaked black on buff.
Do not paint dark legs or a thick bill.
